findings.text: blocking: dataclasses.replace(..., stdin_text="") clears the plan's stdin on the over-ceiling route. Every dialect inherits stdin_prompt=True (reckon/_backends.py:1021), so _backends.py:2230 puts the worker's prompt on stdin (stdin_text=prompt), and the launch feeds it with input=plan.stdin_text (reckon/crew/resumption.py:567); replacing it with "" means a worker declared above 48 GB launches with an empty prompt, so the ceiling route cannot deliver a working worker and the goal's own-job clause is inert in practice. The command is now passed as argv to srun, which forwards the caller's stdin to the task, so the text should be preserved as the normal step branch leaves it. The node's tests cannot catch this because _plan() carries stdin_text="" and the live check ran /bin/echo.

follow-on: the default-bound assertion compares argv against f"--mem={placement.DEFAULT_STEP_MEMORY_GB}G", the same constant the code under test reads at reckon/crew/placement.py:434-438 (also at :93 and :208), so both sides move together and this assertion stays green if the default leaves 24 GB. It is rescued by tests/test_fleet_node.py:480 and :492, which hardcode "--mem=24G" against the composed argv, so the value is independently pinned there; the assertion here should still name an independent 24 GB.

follow-on: the ceiling-routing assertions compare against placement.debug_partition() and placement.DEBUG_PARTITION_SUFFIX on both sides (:115-116), so a regression that changed the _debug suffix or the partition name would move the code and the assertion together and never redden; the partition this route lands on is observed only in the live check log, not pinned by a test.

follow-on: reckon/crew/summary.py is outside the node's recorded write_paths (the dispatch fence names placement.py, fleet_node.py, fleet_migrate.py, dispatch_launch.py, project_setup_commands.py and two test files only) and is flagged by check-manifest; the edit was directed by the coordinator's resume advice to make one reader the owner and have summary.py call it, so the record needs its write scope widened rather than the change reverted.

follow-on: memory_figure_bytes (with _MEMORY_UNIT_BYTES) parses a scheduler memory string to a size, the capability reckon/crew/fleet_node.py:261 parse_memory_gb (with _MEMORY_UNIT_MB) already owns for the same K/M/G/T vocabulary and the same bare-number-means-megabytes rule; they differ only in return unit (bytes vs whole GB) and tolerance, so the parser is duplicated rather than shared. The change does consolidate the other duplicate — summary.py's _option_values and _as_bytes now call placement.option_values and placement.declared_memory_bytes — so the net count of parsers is unchanged.
